subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - Fintech AI / SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - Fintech AI / SLOs

Hi Nina - thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of requirements (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 generation latency target of <= 250ms (streaming responses required for progressive token delivery)
- Concurrency: sustained 50 concurrent live streams during peak (burst to 80 for <10 minutes)
- Throughput: batch embedding/reranking workload ~300 qps off-peak, spiky to ~600 qps for short windows
- Model: preference for an open LLM variant you can host; currently evaluating opt-level equivalent to 70B with quantized execution
- Reliability/SLO: 99.9% uptime, graceful fallback to smaller model when headroom exhausted

Proposed validation approach (next steps):
1) Redwood runs a dedicated-capacity performance validation for a 48-hour window using a configuration we believe will meet your SLOs (see proposed GPU sizing attached).
2) We'll run traffic that mirrors your real distribution (streaming simulated, concurrent streams, batch embedding jobs) and measure p50/p95/p99, tail latency on streaming start, and token throughput.
3) We'll share the raw logs and a summary report (latency heatmaps, concurrency charts, cost estimate).

Questions we have now:
- Can you confirm the p95 requirement is for end-to-end streaming start-to-first-token or full-response p95?
- Are there any regulatory constraints on model variants / on-prem requirements for this proof?
- Who is the procurement contact for a short dedicated capacity trial (billing/PO)?

Attachments: gpu-sizing-estimate-fintech.xlsx (proposed configs), redwood-dedicated-benchmarks-march2026.pdf (reference results)

If that looks right I can schedule the validation window as early as next week. I recommend we plan for a short sync between your perf team and our SEs to lock the test traffic profile - would Wed or Thu work?

Thanks,

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@fintech.ai>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - Fintech AI / SLOs

Thanks, Aditya - this recap is helpful and mostly accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the primary SLO is end-to-end p95 for the full response <= 250ms for short prompts (<128 tokens). For long-form generation (>512 tokens) we care about streaming start time (we want first token in <150ms) and steady-state token cadence.
- Concurrency: 50 sustained real-time streams is correct. During peak trading hours we could see up to 80 concurrent for short bursts (5-10 mins).
- Throughput: batch embedding pipeline currently processes ~300 qps, needs to scale to ~600 qps for promotions; batch windows are OK as long as processing completes within 15 mins.
- Model constraints: we prefer an open checkpoint; also need to validate outputs for potential hallucination risk (will share a small eval set).

Procurement: cc'd is our procurement alias perf-team@fintech.ai - they handle trial PO approval.

Next steps for us:
- Please propose concrete GPU configs and expected headroom/costs.
- We'll schedule a 30-min sync with your SEs to finalize traffic profile (Wed 11-11:30 PST works).

Thanks,
Nina
Director of Product | Fintech AI
nina.patel@fintech.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@fintech.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - Fintech AI / SLOs

Hi Nina - looping in some initial sizing thoughts before the sync. I attached the benchmark PDF and an XLS with a few configuration options. High level takeaways and tradeoffs:

1) GPU choice (A100 vs H100):
   - H100 gives better latency headroom and throughput for decoder-heavy, long-context streaming workloads (especially for quantized FP8/AMP flows). Expect ~20-35% lower p95 latency vs A100 for the same model & sequence length.
   - A100 still a strong cost/perf option for pure batch embedding throughput; if you prioritize embedding cost over streaming latency you can mix node types.

2) Reserved throughput / sizing recommendation (to meet your targets):
   - Baseline: 4x H100 configured with continuous batching + prefix KV cache: should meet p95 <= 250ms for <128-token prompts and first-token <150ms for streaming in our synthetic replay.
   - Headroom: add 1 extra H100 for burst to 80 concurrent streams (hot standby); alternatively use burstable dedicated nodes if you want lower base cost.

3) Streaming considerations:
   - Streaming start time is heavily influenced by model compilation + kernel selection for short prompts - we'll warm kernels during validation and measure cold vs warm starts.
   - Network and TLS handshakes: we recommend persistent connections (HTTP/2) for real-time streams to reduce start latency.

4) Measurement plan for validation run:
   - We'll run sustained load to validate steady-state concurrency and run bursts for 10-minute windows to validate headroom.
   - Collect p50/p95/p99 for token latency, start-of-stream latency, end-to-end response time, and throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec).

Next steps: if you confirm the H100 baseline, we'll provision a 48-hour dedicated cluster and kick off the validation. I can present a cost estimate in the sync.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Thanks, Dylan and Nina - great. Confirming next steps from Redwood side:

1) Provision 48-hour dedicated validation using 5x H100 (4 baseline + 1 burst) with KV cache and continuous batching enabled.
2) Validation schedule: Wed 11 Mar 2026 02:00-14:00 PST (we'll run steady-state + a set of burst windows; details in the test plan we will share).
3) Deliverables: raw latency logs, summary report (p50/p95/p99), cost and sizing recommendation, and follow-up meeting to go over results.

Action items for Fintech AI:
- Confirm acceptance of the 5x H100 config for the trial (reply-all).
- Procurement to approve short-term PO for trial (cc'd perf-team).
- Share the eval prompt set and any restricted-model constraints (if any) by EOD Wed so we can seed the validation traffic appropriately.

I'll lock the calendar for the validation window after procurement thumbs-up. Appreciate the quick turnaround - we'll aim to make the validation as frictionless as possible.

Best,
